newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas gave a response from Commission President Jacques Santer to an invitation by Sir James Goldsmith of Britain's Referendum Party to have a television debate. Santer said he was not at Goldsmith's beck and call and that the proper forum for Goldsmith to debate European questions was the European Parliament, where Goldsmith is a member.
Spokesman Jochen Kubosch said EU and Japanese negotiators had just agreed to increase by 13,000 the number of Japanese car exports allowed into the EU in 1996 -- to 1,079,000.

In response to a question, spokesman Patrick Child said the Commission would not launch internal national debates about how to measure budget deficits. Its role was to guarantee strict implementation of the integrated accounting system established by agreement of all EU states.
Van der Pas said the Commission had received the Court of Auditors report on DGXXIII and was working on its response.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/938: European conference on rural development
- IP/96/939: Edith Cresson on official visit in Russia. Towards a scientific and technological cooperation accord between the European Union and Russia
- Speech/96/252: "Poland's road to the European Union" by Commissioner Hans van den Broek
- Speech/96/253: "The Information Society: New Risks and Opportunities for Privacy", extracts of a speech by Commissioner Mario Monti
- Speech/96/255: "EMU - Why It's Right to Bide our Time" by Sir Leon Brittan
- Speech by Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy at the inauguration of the Investment Forum
- "Europe in the 21st Century: Submit or Act" by Commission President Jacques Santer
